pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMILES AND METAPHORS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What makes short stories interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use similes and metaphors in their own sentences
2. explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMILES AND METAPHORS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMILES AND METAPHORS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use similes and metaphors in their own sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use similes and metaphors in their own sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use similes and metaphors in their own sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use similes and metaphors in their own sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use similes and metaphors in their own sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors to a partner. (skill: explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use similes and metaphors in their own sentences.
3. Practise this skill: explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes short stories interesting?
2. Why should short stories be read?
3. How can one write a short story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.4.1 Intensive Reading: Similes and metaphors means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use similes and metaphors in their own sentences.
5. Be able to: explain the similes and metaphors used in the short story.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
